project.name: Eigenflow
project.objective: Build a PyTorch-first, architecture-agnostic, metric-agnostic post hoc neural-network interpretability toolkit for controlled probe experiments on the relational organization of learned representations across network depth and control scale.
project.interpretive_goal: Extract structural features of learned representations so human experimenters can make empirical inferences about latent representational features.
project.primary_output_objective: Produce a ZIP archive containing a complete initial Eigenflow Git repository, including its .git directory/history, suitable for immediate use as the project repository.

included: Probe-population preparation and experimental design utilities
PyTorch model inspection and activation extraction via standard module hooks
Population-level representation capture across selected or default-eligible internal modules
Metric abstraction and built-in similarity/distance metrics
Filtration abstraction and built-in graph-family constructions
Factor/class alignment analysis using probe metadata
Cross-layer, cross-metric, cross-filtration, cross-model, cross-checkpoint, and cross-probe comparison
PCSCS compatibility as a canonical special-case preset
deferred_not_required_for_v1: Exotic graph operators beyond the initial defined set
Aggressive performance optimization beyond clean sparse-capable architecture

success_criteria.statement: A user can define a probe population, supply a PyTorch model, choose or configure a metric and filtration, select analyses, and run a reproducible experiment end-to-end.
The analysis core does not require model-architecture-specific logic after representations have been extracted.
The same representation population can be analyzed under multiple metrics, filtrations, graph operators, and structural analyses without re-extracting activations.
PCSCS can be represented as a preset/configuration within the general framework rather than as a separate incompatible implementation.
Results preserve sufficient provenance and dependency information to support comparison, regeneration, selective invalidation, and resumption.
The package supports population-level analysis across network depth and control scale, producing structural observables Q(layer, control_parameter).
The final deliverable can be unzipped and immediately used as a Git repository with package source, tests, documentation, examples, project-state artifacts, and coherent initial commit history.

A first-time technically competent analyst or neural-network systems architect can progress through the human-facing surface to justified competence in deciding when/how to use Eigenflow and in producing bounded, human-interpretable inferences about internal representation from experimental outputs.

constraints.statement: PyTorch handles model-specific forward execution; Eigenflow wraps extraction and performs architecture-independent downstream analysis.
Do not require the package to infer semantic meaning of arbitrary internal modules automatically.
Structural observables are empirical evidence about latent feature organization, not automatic semantic explanations.
Percolation terminology must distinguish descriptive percolation-style observables from stronger claims of literal criticality or universality.
Spectral eigenvector tracking must account for crossings and degeneracies using eigenspace-aware correspondence rather than naive sorted-index identity.
v1 should be conceptually complete rather than intentionally minimal.

terminology.definition: A deliberately constructed set of model inputs, optionally with metadata and controlled factors, used as an experimental instrument for post hoc interpretability.
An internal PyTorch module/output location where activations for the entire probe population are captured. User-facing language may say 'layer' where appropriate.
The collection Z^(l) of vector representations of all probes at one internal site l.
The pairwise similarity, distance, affinity, or kernel structure induced over a representation population by a chosen metric.
A parameterized family of graphs or weighted relational structures generated from a relational matrix as a control parameter varies.
A measurable property of a representation-induced graph/operator family, such as component count, giant-component fraction, susceptibility, spectral gap, IPR, or factor alignment.
A structural feature of the learned representation geometry/topology, used as evidence about first-kind latent representational features.
A latent feature or organizing representational property learned by the neural network, inferred indirectly from controlled structural evidence.

decisions.decision: Eigenflow is PyTorch-first for v1.
decisions.rationale: PyTorch already performs model-specific execution and exposes generic module inspection and forward hooks.

decisions.decision: Downstream analysis is architecture-agnostic after activation extraction.
decisions.rationale: The scientific core operates on population representation matrices rather than model internals.

decisions.decision: The default analytical object is the relational organization of the entire probe population at each internal site, not single-input activation trajectories.
The principal domain is a two-dimensional layer-by-control space, with observables Q(l, p).
Probe design is a first-class subsystem, because the probe population is an experimental instrument.
Metric and filtration are separate abstractions.
Edge density is a first-class canonical control coordinate for cross-metric comparison where applicable.
Spectral analysis is operator-based and not synonymous with Laplacian analysis.
PCSCS remains a named canonical special case/preset within Eigenflow.
v1 should implement the full conceptual architecture rather than an intentionally narrow core.
The package should support preparation/configuration tools for probe populations, metrics, and filtrations rather than only accepting prebuilt objects.
Raw structural observations and interpretive claims remain explicitly separated.
The primary project deliverable is a ZIP archive of the complete initial Eigenflow Git repository, including the .git directory and usable commit history.
decisions.rationale: The repository itself is the durable implementation artifact; specifications, documentation, tests, and examples should live inside and evolve with it.

decisions.rationale: Documentation completeness is defined by the reader states and evidential judgments it enables, not by topical coverage alone.

decisions.decision: The default activation reducer for v1 alpha is flatten; reducer choice is part of the measurement definition.
decisions.rationale: Resolved from implemented package behavior during documentation reconciliation.

decisions.decision: The implemented v1 alpha metric and graph-operator sets documented in the package are the reference built-in sets for this release; operator additions that change scientific semantics require project-state, changelog, tests, and documentation synchronization.
decisions.rationale: Updated after signed-graph compatibility work added explicit signed Laplacian operators while preserving the operator-based spectral architecture.

decisions.decision: Visualization is an epistemic interface organized by analyst questions and evidential tier, not a collection of statistic-specific plot helpers.

decisions.rationale: Visualization ontology implementation phase.

decisions.decision: PCSCS visualization parity is a required baseline, generalized by Eigenflow component, percolation, spectral, eigenspace, factor, layer×control, robustness, and interpretation views.
decisions.rationale: Visualization ontology implementation phase.

decisions.decision: Canonical visualization documentation must pair real generated output with code, intended use, permitted inference, alternatives, and common misinterpretation.
decisions.rationale: Visualization ontology implementation phase.

decisions.decision: Graph operators declare and enforce mathematical compatibility requirements before numerical construction; unsupported graph/operator pairings are represented as structured incompatibilities rather than allowed to propagate NaN/Inf or opaque linear-algebra failures.
decisions.rationale: Package-wide pressure testing exposed signed weighted graphs reaching ordinary normalized degree operators. The relational measurement is valid, but the operator semantics are not. Compatibility therefore belongs at the graph/operator boundary.

decisions.decision: Signed relational graphs remain first-class measurements. Eigenflow does not silently clip, shift, or absolutize negative weights; deliberate signed spectral analysis uses explicit signed_laplacian or signed_normalized_laplacian operators based on absolute weighted degree.
decisions.rationale: Negative cosine/dot-product similarities are legitimate experimental outcomes. Silent coercion would alter the measurement semantics.

decisions.decision: Eigenspace overlap and principal-angle trajectories require a common ambient space. Operators such as non-backtracking that act in filtration-dependent directed-edge spaces return structured changing_ambient_space incompatibility records unless an explicit alignment method is supplied.
decisions.rationale: Pressure testing showed that non-backtracking spectra are valid while naive cross-snapshot eigenspace products fail when edge-space dimension changes.

decisions.decision: Complex-spectrum support uses one primary public keyword complex= with values auto, preserve, modulus, real, phase, imag, and error.
decisions.rationale: Minimize API syntax while allowing researchers to state the interpretation they actually intend.

decisions.decision: complex="auto" is the default. Effectively real spectra remain silent; genuinely complex spectra are preserved and trigger concise actionable guidance when no treatment was declared.
decisions.rationale: Avoid burdening ordinary users while preventing silent scientific assumptions.

decisions.decision: Raw complex eigenvalues/eigenvectors remain canonical under every policy; scalar treatments are derived analytical views, never destructive transforms.
decisions.rationale: Preserves evidence and supports later reinterpretation without recomputation.

decisions.decision: Operator spectral expectations are internal metadata, not additional user syntax.
decisions.rationale: Distinguish expected from surprising complex spectra without API expansion.

decisions.decision: Existing spectral visualizations adapt to the selected complex policy; one additional canonical complex-plane visualization is added rather than a family of plotting APIs.
decisions.rationale: Keep visualization discoverability high and syntax compact.

decisions.decision: Complex eigenvalue trajectories use explicit cross-snapshot matching in the complex plane; sorted eigenvalue index is not treated as mode identity.
decisions.rationale: Prevents false continuity through crossings and complex-plane rearrangements.

decisions.decision: Pseudospectra, full nonnormal transient-growth analysis, directed-edge eigenspace alignment, research-preset objects, and complex-specific configuration classes remain deferred.
decisions.rationale: Deliver scientifically safe complex support without anticipatory API or computational complexity.

decisions.decision: Unexpected complex spectra for expected-real operators are diagnostics rather than automatically harmless or fatal; complex="error" is the explicit strict-assumption mode.
decisions.rationale: Preserve evidence while making assumption violations visible.

decisions.decision: Formal planning is a canonical-state operation requiring dependency/downstream/API/docs/tests analysis, executable units, synchronized manifest mutation, provenance, and validation.
decisions.rationale: User explicitly defined formal planning as persistent project governance rather than conversational planning.

assumptions.statement: Most v1 users will provide standard PyTorch nn.Module models whose useful internal activations are hookable.
A default broad capture policy can be defined, but actual scientific analysis may need filtering to avoid trivial or redundant modules.
Flatten can remain available for PCSCS compatibility, but no single representation reducer should be treated as scientifically universal.

unresolved_questions.question: What exact public Python API and protocol/interface signatures should be frozen for v1?
unresolved_questions.resolution: Resolved from implemented v1 alpha API. Experiment(model, probes, metric='cosine', filtration='edge_density', analyses=['components','percolation','spectra'], extraction=ExtractionConfig(), device=None, collate_fn=None); exact subordinate interfaces are now documented in docs/spec/API_SPEC.md.

unresolved_questions.question: What is the default module-capture policy for arbitrary PyTorch models: literally all hookable modules, filtered eligible modules, or named structural boundaries?
unresolved_questions.resolution: Default arbitrary-PyTorch capture policy is all named leaf nn.Module objects when ExtractionConfig(sites='all', leaf_modules_only=True). Explicit site names override the default.

unresolved_questions.question: What is the default representation reduction behavior when module outputs are not already 2D sample-by-feature matrices?
unresolved_questions.resolution: Default representation reduction is flatten. Alternative implemented reducers include global_average, global_max, MeanTokens, SelectToken object, and callables.

unresolved_questions.question: Which built-in metrics and kernels are mandatory for v1 versus extension candidates?
unresolved_questions.resolution: The v1 alpha built-in metric set is cosine, Euclidean, squared Euclidean, Manhattan, correlation, dot product, Mahalanobis, RBF, polynomial, callable metrics, plus MetricPipeline transforms.

unresolved_questions.question: Which graph operators are mandatory for v1, particularly whether modularity and non-backtracking belong in the initial release?
unresolved_questions.resolution: The v1 alpha operator set is adjacency, combinatorial Laplacian, normalized Laplacian, random walk, modularity, and non-backtracking.

unresolved_questions.question: What result serialization format and compatibility policy should be used for long-lived experiment artifacts?
unresolved_questions.resolution: Current persistence is JSON-only through ExperimentResult.save(); eigenvectors are omitted, there is no public load/reconstruction API, and alpha compatibility requires retaining package version/configuration.

unresolved_questions.question: How should analysis keyword aliases map to explicit typed analysis configurations?
unresolved_questions.resolution: Analysis strings resolve to default Analysis objects. Non-default configuration is expressed by passing explicit typed Analysis instances. This mapping is documented in API_SPEC.md.

objective_reader_state.statement: The reader can make informed, justified decisions about whether and how to use Eigenflow in neural-network feature-interpretation experiments, can design the experiment so its outputs bear on an explicit interpretive question, and can interpret those outputs in a manner consistent with the experimental design, the intrinsic scope of each observable, and the distinction between structural evidence and claims about latent features.

competencies.statement: Determine whether an interpretability question is suitable for a probe-population relational experiment and identify what evidence would count for or against the relevant hypotheses.
Construct a probe population whose manipulated factors, controls, balance, metadata, and contrasts make the intended inference identifiable enough to be scientifically useful.
Choose representation sites/reducers, similarity or distance metrics, and filtration/control coordinates for reasons connected to the hypothesis rather than convenience alone.
Configure and execute an Eigenflow experiment using the actual public API and inspect the resulting structured outputs.

Explain what component, percolation, spectral/eigenspace, factor-alignment, bridge, k-core, community, and transition observables measure and what patterns they can reveal about representation populations.
Translate structural patterns into bounded candidate interpretations of latent feature organization while identifying alternative explanations and unsupported claims.
Use convergent evidence and robustness checks across layers, metrics, reducers, filtrations, sample sizes, and probe manipulations to strengthen or weaken an interpretation.
Produce a human-interpretable experimental account connecting the original hypothesis, probe design, observed structural changes, robustness evidence, and justified conclusion.

content_rules: Every major concept page must state indication: when the concept is useful and what question it answers.

tiers.name: primary evidential
tiers.purpose: Expose measured relational/structural evidence directly and support substantive experimental inference.

tiers.name: diagnostic

views.name: Probe design / factor structure view
views.question: Does the probe population actually distinguish the experimental hypotheses?
views.encoding: factor-count bars, factorial contingency heatmap, missing-cell indicators, optional sample gallery
views.permitted_inference: Assess balance, coverage, factorial completeness, and obvious confounding in the probe design.
views.common_misinterpretation: Treating balanced counts as proof that all nuisance variables are controlled.

views.name: Factor-ordered relational matrix
views.question: What pairwise relational geometry exists before graph thresholding, and how does it align with known factors?
views.encoding: heatmap ordered or annotated by experimental factors
views.permitted_inference: Identify broad block structure, gradients, outliers, and factor-consistent relational organization under the chosen metric.
views.common_misinterpretation: Treating visible blocks as metric-independent latent classes.

views.name: Connected-component trajectory
views.question: How does fragmentation collapse as the control parameter changes?
views.encoding: component count vs control parameter; optional smoothed curve; critical and convergence annotations
views.permitted_inference: Locate regimes of rapid merger, persistence, and global convergence.
views.common_misinterpretation: Equating the maximal derivative with a physical critical point or semantic transition without supporting evidence.

views.name: Component membership raster
views.question: Which probes remain grouped together across control scale?
views.encoding: probe × control matrix colored by component identity, optionally ordered by factor
views.permitted_inference: Assess persistence, group stability, and which probes change membership relationships across scale.
views.common_misinterpretation: Interpreting component color identity as stable semantic labels when components merge and labels may be arbitrary.

views.name: Merge-event plot
views.question: Which groups merge, at what control values, and through which relations?
views.encoding: event timeline/tree with source and resulting components
views.permitted_inference: Identify discrete merger events and candidate bridge relations driving larger-scale consolidation.
views.common_misinterpretation: Assuming one merge event corresponds to one semantic feature transition.

views.name: Dendrogram / merge hierarchy
views.question: What hierarchical order of relational consolidation is induced by the filtration?
views.encoding: hierarchical tree with branch height tied to filtration/native threshold quantity
views.permitted_inference: Visualize persistent relational groupings and their merge order.
views.common_misinterpretation: Treating the graph filtration as identical to standard agglomerative clustering or treating branch heights as metric-independent semantic distances.

views.name: Percolation / structural-transition dashboard
views.question: How does graph structure move from local fragmentation to mesoscale and macroscopic connectivity?
views.encoding: aligned component count, giant component, second component, susceptibility, transition markers
views.permitted_inference: Characterize graph-growth regimes and compare multiple transition indicators.
views.common_misinterpretation: Calling finite-sample transition markers universal phase transitions.

views.name: Graph snapshot with semantic annotation
views.question: What does one selected graph state look like, and which probes/edges are structurally important?
views.encoding: node-link layout colored by factor/community/core with highlighted bridges
views.permitted_inference: Inspect local structural roles and identify probes worth qualitative examination.
views.common_misinterpretation: Reading force-directed node position as a learned embedding or metric geometry.

views.name: Static eigenvalue spectrum
views.question: What operator-scale structure exists at a selected graph state?
views.encoding: eigenvalue index/value plot with operator and control annotations
views.permitted_inference: Inspect zero modes, algebraic connectivity, spectral gaps, spectral concentration, and operator-specific structure.
views.common_misinterpretation: Assigning semantic meaning to isolated eigenvalues without probe/factor context.

views.name: Spectral flow
views.question: How do operator eigenvalues change across the filtration?
views.encoding: multiple eigenvalue branches vs control parameter
views.permitted_inference: Identify persistent spectral regimes, crossings, gap openings/closures, and scale-dependent operator structure.
views.common_misinterpretation: Assuming sorted eigenvalue index identifies the same eigenmode across crossings or degeneracy.

views.name: Spectral-properties dashboard
views.question: How do key spectral observables jointly characterize structural organization across control scale?
views.encoding: aligned algebraic connectivity, selected gaps, entropy/effective rank, energy, localization/IPR, transition annotations
views.permitted_inference: Compare complementary spectral summaries and align them with structural transition regimes.
views.common_misinterpretation: Treating all spectral statistics as interchangeable measures of one latent property.

views.name: Eigenspace stability view
views.question: Are low-dimensional structural modes stable across adjacent control values?
views.encoding: principal-angle trajectories and overlap heatmaps
views.permitted_inference: Assess subspace continuity through eigenvalue crossings or near-degeneracy.
views.common_misinterpretation: Treating an individual basis vector as stable when only the subspace is identified.

views.name: Factor-alignment trajectory
views.question: How strongly does emergent graph structure align with controlled semantic factors across scale?
views.encoding: NMI/ARI vs control parameter for one or more factors
views.permitted_inference: Compare which recorded factors best explain emergent component partitions under the current design.
views.common_misinterpretation: Treating high alignment as proof of unique semantic encoding or causality.

views.name: Factor internal-vs-external connectivity
views.question: Are probes within a factor level more densely connected than they are to other levels?
views.encoding: internal and external edge-density trajectories by factor level
views.permitted_inference: Assess relational coherence and mixing of controlled groups.
views.common_misinterpretation: Interpreting group separation as universally desirable or as sufficient evidence of a causal feature.

views.name: Layer × control heatmap
views.question: Where in network depth and relational scale does a structural observable change?
views.encoding: site/layer × control heatmap
views.permitted_inference: Locate depth-dependent emergence, strengthening, weakening, or movement of structural regimes.
views.common_misinterpretation: Treating non-equivalent sites across architectures as metrically interchangeable.

views.name: Combined-layer dynamics
views.question: How do the same structural trajectories compare across representation sites?
views.encoding: multi-layer overlays or aligned small multiples
views.permitted_inference: Compare persistence, transition location, and structural strength through depth.
views.common_misinterpretation: Comparing native metric thresholds across layers or metrics when scales are not commensurable.

views.name: Bridge/core/outlier diagnostic
views.question: Which individual probes disproportionately influence structural connectivity or spectral organization?
views.encoding: probe ranking, probe trajectory, highlighted graph nodes, optional image/contact sheet
views.permitted_inference: Identify structurally pivotal or atypical probes for qualitative inspection.
views.common_misinterpretation: Assuming an influential probe is mislabeled or semantically ambiguous without inspecting it.

views.name: Measurement robustness comparison
views.question: Does the substantive interpretation survive reasonable changes in metric, reducer, filtration, or probe sample?
views.encoding: matched-control overlays, robustness matrices, difference heatmaps, resampling intervals
views.permitted_inference: Assess dependence of conclusions on analysis choices and finite-sample variation.
views.common_misinterpretation: Treating numerical non-identity as failure when the substantive structural conclusion is stable.

views.name: Cross-model / cross-condition comparison
views.question: How does representational organization differ between models, checkpoints, or interventions?
views.encoding: difference heatmaps, aligned trajectories, model × layer summaries
views.permitted_inference: Compare structural consequences of training state, architecture, or intervention under matched probe designs.
views.common_misinterpretation: Attributing differences to architecture/training when probe preprocessing or site alignment also changed.

views.name: Integrated experimental-interpretation dashboard
views.question: What combined visual evidence bears directly on the experiment's feature-interpretation hypothesis?
views.encoding: curated panel combining factor alignment, structural transition, layer×control, selected graph, and robustness evidence
views.permitted_inference: Synthesize complementary evidence into a bounded experimental conclusion.
views.common_misinterpretation: Treating the dashboard as an automated explanation rather than a structured evidence display.

development_instrumentation_phase.name: Development Instrumentation and Longitudinal Representation Analysis
development_instrumentation_phase.objective: Extend Eigenflow from a single-model representation experiment engine into a first-class representation observability system for architecture development, fine-tuning, checkpoint analysis, PEFT targeting, dataset diagnosis, retention/forgetting analysis, and longitudinal model-development workflows.
governing_principles: Preserve Experiment -> ExperimentResult as the atomic measurement layer.
Add higher-order abstractions above ExperimentResult rather than replacing the core experiment engine.
Treat longitudinal and cross-model comparisons as controlled experiments, not arbitrary result subtraction.
Require compatibility validation before structural comparisons are interpreted.
Keep probe design and measurement configuration explicit, versioned, and reproducible.
Do not collapse representation structure into a universal quality score.
Keep behavioral performance, computational efficiency, and representation structure as distinct evidence channels.
Documentation and implementation must evolve together and remain implementation-faithful.
target_use_cases: architecture-stage analysis and localization of meaningful representation change
architecture comparison under matched probe designs
bottleneck, residual, attention, and module-level structural diagnosis
checkpoint trajectories and Q(layer, control, time)
PEFT / LoRA / adapter targeting and comparison
structural early stopping and checkpoint selection
development dashboards combining behavior, efficiency, and representation structure

change_plans.title: First-class complex-spectrum support without public-API explosion
change_plans.problem_statement: Eigenflow must preserve and support genuinely complex spectra across research workflows while keeping ordinary real-spectrum usage simple. Researchers who expect complex values need one compact treatment option; researchers who do not expect them need actionable diagnostics rather than silent coercion or excessive configuration.
researcher_outcomes: A researcher studying an operator such as non-backtracking can state the intended complex interpretation with one keyword.
A researcher using expected-real operators sees no extra complexity unless a materially complex spectrum actually appears.
Unexpected complex values are preserved and surfaced with enough diagnostic context to decide whether they are mathematically meaningful, numerically suspicious, or assumption-violating.
Visualizations, comparisons, trajectories, persistence, and summaries remain semantically consistent with the selected treatment.
Publication/reproducibility artifacts retain the raw complex evidence and the policy/provenance used to summarize it.

non_goals: No destructive projection of stored eigenvalues.

behavior.auto: Silent for effectively real spectra. For genuinely complex spectra, preserve raw values, emit concise actionable guidance, and skip summaries that require an undeclared scalar ordering.
behavior.preserve: Treat complex spectra as intentional; compute only intrinsically complex-safe summaries unless a projection is explicitly requested elsewhere.
behavior.modulus: Use |lambda| for scalar ordering, gap-like summaries, default 1-D trajectories and comparisons while preserving raw lambda.
behavior.real: Use Re(lambda) for scalar ordering and compatible summaries while preserving raw lambda.
behavior.phase: Use arg(lambda) for phase-oriented summaries/trajectories with circular semantics and unwrapping after mode matching.
behavior.imag: Use Im(lambda) for scalar treatment when explicitly requested; supported but not emphasized as a generic scientific interpretation.
behavior.error: Raise an explicit assumption violation when a genuinely complex spectrum is detected.

internal_semantics.complex_detection: Classify meaningfully complex using absolute + relative tolerance; persist the chosen tolerances and diagnostics.

conditionally_real: random_walk under current undirected nonnegative graph assumptions

internal_semantics.canonical_storage: Complex eigenvalues/eigenvectors are authoritative. real/imag/modulus/phase are derived views.
complex_safe_math: Hermitian inner products and subspace operations
scalar_semantics: generic gap semantics must not silently change
projection-specific gaps must be explicitly named/typed
trajectory_semantics: match modes across adjacent snapshots by complex-plane assignment rather than sorted index
eigenvalue tracking remains separate from eigenspace tracking when operator ambient dimension changes
